Challis, C.E. (2020). Process energy efficiency and human factors in dairy pasteurisation and other "black box" processes. EngD thesis (Systems), Faculty of Engineering, University of Bristol; submitted September 2019, deposited February 2020; industrial sponsor Verco. University of Bristol Research Portal, http://research-information.bristol.ac.uk

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 1). Used in place of the unobtainable Carbon Trust CTG033 dairy guide (user ruling 2026-10-07). Main file: measured pasteuriser data from three plants at two UK dairy sites (author analysis of SCADA/data-logger data): site Y cream pasteuriser P2 (20 m3/h, 90 degC, regeneration 82-87%, hot-water heat 11.1-13.3 kWh/m3); site Z yoghurt unit P7 (20 m3/h, 95 degC, apparent regeneration about 61% (53-65%), steam-derived heat about 59 kWh/m3; a poor old unit); site Z P5 skim (74%) and P6 cream (86%; 89-91% falling to low 80s) efficiency only; achievable regeneration 90-92% (Carbon Trust 2010) and 95% (Tetra Pak 2017) as heat-exchanger_steam-heated_efficiency-strong. Heat figures are delivered hot-water heat, not boiler fuel. Cooling (chilled water) demand, CIP energy per clean, kW figures without flow and sector statistics are in _other-values; operational savings (running-cost savings priced with the author 2017 energy-price assumptions; no capital costs anywhere) in _measures. NOT duplicated here because they are extracted under challis_2017_001 (the thesis Sect. 3.2 reproduces that paper): the CTG033 pasteuriser pair (93%/2.5 and 88%/3.55 kgCO2e/m3), +1% regeneration = 0.2 kgCO2e/m3 and GBP 10,100/yr, excess water recirculation +16-18%, Fig. 3-1 (specific CO2 of raw-milk processes) and Fig. 3-2 (dairy kWh/m3 best/average/worst) - thesis p.92-93 and p.122. Traps: Table 4-2 prints 0.0112 kWh/L beside the 266 kW row (should be 0.0133; kW/flow used); CIP hot/cold totals swapped between listing and use (p.195-196); Table 4-11 R2in/R2out labels look swapped against the text. No capital costs; no evaporator, spray-dryer or refrigeration-plant numbers (evaporators mentioned only qualitatively, p.312).
